;;;; after.lisp.txt --- the post-fix shape of before.lisp.txt, kept as a fixture
;;;; so the scanner in lisptemppath_class_test.go can be shown to say nothing
;;;; about it (nova-tools#1699). Not loaded by anything: it is data for a Go test.
;;;;
;;;; Its COMMENTS quote the banned constructs on purpose -- this line names
;;;; uiop:default-temporary-directory, (sb-posix:getenv "TMPDIR"), #p"/tmp/" and
;;;; (random 1000000) -- because a scanner that could not tell code from a
;;;; comment would need an allowlist entry for every paragraph that told the
;;;; truth. The docstrings below say the same things in words instead, because
;;;; string literals stay visible to the scanner: that is where a real offending
;;;; path lives.

(in-package #:nova-work/tests)

(defun test-journal-path (name)
  "A journal path under this run's own root. It used to be built from the
shared temporary directory, a fixed sub-directory name, the universal time and
a counter that starts at zero in every image."
  (test-temp-file name "journal"))

(defun dedup-root-temp-dir ()
  "A fresh 0700 directory under this run's own root, the one place this file
writes. It used to read the TMPDIR environment variable directly."
  (test-temp-dir "dedup-root"))

(defun %request-line-dir ()
  "A fresh 0700 directory for one endpoint, named on this run's short tag. It
used to be a fixed name under the system temporary directory."
  (let ((dir (merge-pathnames (concatenate 'string (test-short-tag "reqline") "/")
                              (test-run-root))))
    (ensure-directories-exist dir)
    dir))

(deftest "endpoint-is-local-and-private" "docs/SPEC-WORK.md:5727" "expected=x"
  (let ((base (test-short-tag "s05-endpoint")))
    (ok base "a base")))
